chunks: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Ten people killed one man.' He said: 'If his next of kin wish, they may kill them all together, and [the killers' families] pay nine blood-monies; or if they wish, they may select one man and kill him, while the remaining nine each pay one-tenth of the blood-money to the family of the last one killed.' He said: 'Thereafter, the ruler takes charge of disciplining them and imprisoning them.'

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاء: Awliya' — the next of kin/guardians who hold the right of retaliation (qisas)
key_terms.الدِّيَة: Diya — blood-money; the financial compensation for unlawful killing
key_terms.الْوَالِي: Al-wali — the ruler or governing authority responsible for public order and discretionary punishment (ta'zir)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when a group of people collectively kill one person?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) rules on the case of ten people who collectively kill one man. The victim's guardians have a choice: execute all ten (with nine blood-monies paid back) or execute one (with the remaining nine each paying one-tenth of the blood-money). The ruler then disciplines and imprisons the perpetrators. This ruling reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential principle that collective killers are all liable, with the guardian having discretion over retaliation and financial compensation.
